content.rationale: the extension shell that hosts the finished page, together with the manifest that names it (uuutyrzs): package.json declares the extension as deccy-viewer, displayed as "Deccy Viewer", contributes the single command deccyViewer.openGraph to the Command Palette and the panel title bar, activates on that command and on a folder that carries nodes/*.json, and keys the title-bar entry on the view type the panel is created with, deccyViewer.graph — the very string src/panel.ts exports as GRAPH_PANEL_VIEW_TYPE, so the manifest's when-condition and the panel's type are one seam rather than two names that can drift apart. src/extension.ts registers the command under the id the manifest contributes, and out/extension.js is the bundle built from those sources, so what the host loads carries the same names as what the manifest says. Nothing here invents viewer behaviour: the page draws the graph (rtlotqvy) and the shell only opens, serves and feeds it. The page the shell opens and serves is the composition's own (tpztomkv): src/panel.ts names media/webview.html as the document it hands the webview, and package.json's build:page compiles the entry point src/webview/main.ts the page runs, so the shell fixes which file is hosted and how it is built and leaves the page's own composition to the node that owns it. package.json declares @vscode/codicons as the only runtime dependency, so the production dependency closure the packager resolves contains nothing beyond it; the build and check-suite tooling (esbuild and the @types packages) stays dev-only and never becomes part of that closure. Beside serving the page, feeding it the graph and keeping its panel state, the shell answers the page's request that a content ref path be opened (rptlovpt): src/panel.ts treats the path the page names as data, resolves it against the workspace root, and answers nothing — reporting the failure through the workbench's error notification — when the resolved path is the root itself, leaves the root (`..` or an absolute path elsewhere), or names no file of it; otherwise it opens the file that path names in the editor. The path is resolved and checked before the editor is asked for anything, so a failure leaves the document the user was reading where it was and opens nothing else, and the node-document open keeps its own double-click seam (trxzsqpv) untouched: the two requests are separate branches of the one message channel.
